subject.title: fix(cron): support current and session: targets in initial delivery resolution

question: Should direct `CronService.add` and declarative-convergence callers implicitly add announce delivery for `current` and `session:*` jobs, or must every supported caller pass through the canonical creation normalizer first?
rationale: Both choices alter persisted delivery behavior for callers that currently bypass normalization, and repository policy requires one canonical path rather than another manually synchronized default matrix.

options.title: Centralize the default policy
options.body: Extract one shared delivery-default resolver used by normalization and direct-service creation, preserving consistent behavior without parallel policy copies.

options.title: Keep normalization as the boundary
options.body: Require direct-service and declarative callers to normalize their create input before persistence and remove implicit service-layer policy beyond that boundary.

options.title: Retain the duplicated fallback
options.body: Accept separate normalization and service conditions, along with the ongoing compatibility and drift risk demonstrated by this inconsistency.

recommendation.title: Centralize the default policy
recommendation.body: Extract one shared delivery-default resolver used by normalization and direct-service creation, preserving consistent behavior without parallel policy copies.

likelyOwner.reason: The persistent-target contract and recent cron service history most directly connect this person to the boundary decision.
